Cleaning steps

The original file is untouched; the cleaned copy adds columns and removes nothing

  1. Purchase frequency had two pairs of labels for the same period. A new column merges Bi-Weekly into Fortnightly and Every 3 Months into Quarterly, relabelling — rows. The original column is kept.
  2. Blank review ratings are flagged in a new column and left blank. Nothing was filled in, so rating figures use rated purchases only.
  3. Promo Code Used matches Discount Applied in — rows, so the two are analysed as one field.
  4. Age group, loyalty segment and estimated purchases per year were added for segmentation.
  5. Whitespace, value ranges and spelling were checked; no other fixes were needed.

Recommendations

Immediate actions
  1. Audit the subscription and discount fields. No female customer is recorded as subscribed or discounted; fix capture before using these fields for targeting.
  2. Review blanket discounts. They reach — of purchases without raising order value; test smaller or targeted offers.
  3. Add order dates and order IDs to the export so trends, repeat rate and lifetime value can be measured.
Short-term improvements
  1. Plan stock and campaigns around —, the strongest season, and use promotions to lift —.
  2. Review —: smallest category with the lowest average order; widen the range or bundle it with Clothing.
  3. Investigate low ratings for — and other bottom-rated products (fit, quality, descriptions).
Long-term strategies
  1. Invest in acquisition. First-time buyers are only — of customers.
  2. Reward the loyal base with tiered benefits beyond discounts, then measure whether subscribers buy more often.
  3. Build a customer lifetime value and demand forecast once per-order, dated history is available.
Definitions and assumptions
Revenue
Sum of Purchase Amount (USD). Each customer has one recorded purchase.
Average order value
Revenue divided by purchases.
Share
A group's revenue as a percentage of the revenue shown.
Loyalty segment
From Previous Purchases: New = 1, Returning = 2–10, Loyal = 11 or more.
Average review rating
Mean of non-blank ratings (1–5 scale; values in the file run from 2.5 to 5.0).
Hypothesis tests
Welch t-tests, one-way ANOVA and chi-square tests run in Python on the full file; p < 0.05 counts as significant.
